(i) the correlativity between duties and rights is non-transitive, (ii) the correlativity of present-rights-of-present persons is the most suitable for legal and political purposes, and (iii) this view can be defended against the NIP.

1) The correlativity of rights and duties is a necessary condition for the possibility of rights; 2) The correlativity is not transitive; 3) Rights can only be held by present persons; and 4) The correlativity condition is satisfied in the present-rights-of-present- persons view.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
correlativity is the key to the debate on the NIP, that correlativity is not a necessary feature of rights and that correlativity is best preserved by adopting a non-transitive rights view.
correlativity in rights and duties is a necessary condition of rights and duties themselves, and the NIP is a necessary condition for correlativity to be preserved in the case of future persons.
the correlativity inherent in rights language is not a reason to dismiss the notion of rights of future people, but rather to adopt a non-transitive view of rights and correlativity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
correlativity is not a feature of rights but of persons and, therefore, the NIP’s challenge to rights of future persons is a challenge to the very notion of future persons.
the NIP is right in its claim that correlativity is not satisfied in the future, and thus rights cannot be attributed to future persons.

the NIP is not only an argument against the idea of future persons having present rights, but also an argument against any view of rights that would not respect the correlativity between present rights and present duties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the correlativity between the right and the duty of the same person is the key to understand how the NIP can preserve rights language when talking about the future.
the idea of rights is a very useful one in the context of the NIP and in the context of future persons, but that it is a very limited idea, which should not be used in a transitive way.
the idea that future people have a right to be born is a non-starter, as it is not possible to have rights of future people.
